candidateAnswers.label: Youth employment by industry
candidateAnswers.position: Use BLS Current Population Survey or OEWS teen-heavy occupations to pick which part-time jobs 14- to 17-year-olds hold, weighted by the town's industry mix once the county file is in, with state rules on hours for minors.

notes: The placeholder is TEEN_PUBLIC_ROLE_PLACEHOLDER in src/simulation/job-market.ts: a library page or recreation aide at the town's county or city government, 8 to 14 hours a week, at the federal minimum of $7.25 an hour.
A town business with part-time staff is used first; none exist on main yet, so every teen first job today is with a public body.
Puerto Rico and the other territories have no public body on file, so no first job is offered there yet.
question: A teenager's first job now comes from the town's own employers. Until town businesses exist, it is one of two placeholder public-body roles (library page or recreation aide) at the federal minimum wage, 8 to 14 hours a week. Which first jobs do 14- to 17-year-olds actually hold, how does that vary by place and industry, what do they pay by state, and what hour limits apply to minors during the school year?

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: It is the federal floor only; state minimums and youth rules are not on file.

title: Which first jobs teenagers hold, and what they pay
usableAnswer: A short list of first jobs by place type or industry, each with a typical hourly pay range by state and its source, plus the hour limits for 14- and 15-year-olds and for 16- and 17-year-olds during the school year.
whyItMatters: Every life that takes a job as a teenager goes through this, and today every one of them is a library page or recreation aide at minimum wage.
